passages.text: Therefore if you occasionally lapse into sin, do not lose heart and cease trying to advance, for God will draw good even out of our falls, like the merchant who sells theriac, who first takes poison, then the theriac, to prove the power of his elixir.
passages.note: Failure and relapse; not losing heart

passages.text: Can any evil be greater than that we find at home? What peace can we hope to find elsewhere, if we have none within us?
passages.note: Seeking peace outside when it is missing within

passages.text: The only remedy for having given up a habit of recollection is to recommence it, otherwise the soul will continue to lose it more and more every day, and God grant it may realize its danger.

What misery to live in this world! We are like men whose enemies are at the door, who must not lay aside their arms, even while sleeping or eating, and are always in dread lest the foe should enter the fortress by some breach in the walls.
passages.note: Constant vigilance and insecurity in life

passages.text: His Majesty knows that I have nothing to rely upon but His mercy; as I cannot cancel the past, I have no other remedy but to flee to Him, and to confide in the merits of His Son and of His Virgin Mother, whose habit, unworthy as I am, I wear as you do also.
passages.note: Regret over the past; relying on mercy
